hints: Choose an instrument designed to measure a length of about one metre directly, without repeatedly repositioning a short scale.
walkthrough: The quantity being measured is the length of a string, and the table shows that it is approximately 126 cm long.
The instrument must therefore measure a length a little greater than one metre directly and with suitable precision.
A metre rule or a tape measure is appropriate.

ai_rubric.observable: Names a metre rule or tape measure as the instrument used to measure the string length.

hints: Before substituting, convert the measured length and mass into metres and kilograms.
Use T = 1.8 N, l = 1.26 m and m = 5.1 × 10⁻³ kg in the supplied square-root expression.
walkthrough: The supplied expression uses SI quantities, so first convert the measurements to SI units.
Convert the length: l = 126 cm = 126 ÷ 100 = 1.26 m.
Convert the mass: m = 5.1 g = 5.1 ÷ 1000 = 5.1 × 10⁻³ kg.
The tension is already in SI units: T = 1.8 N.
Substitute the values into the supplied expression: v = √[(Tl)/m] = √[(1.8 × 1.26)/(5.1 × 10⁻³)].
Calculate the numerator: 1.8 × 1.26 = 2.268.
Divide by the mass: 2.268 ÷ 0.0051 = 444.7.
Take the square root: v = √444.7 = 21.064... m s⁻¹.
Round appropriately to three significant figures: v = 21.1 m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies the supplied relationship using T = 1.8 N, l = 1.26 m and m = 5.1 × 10⁻³ kg, including the necessary SI-unit conversions.
Obtains a wave speed of 21.1 m s⁻¹, or an equivalent correctly rounded value.

hints: The speed is the square root of a product and quotient, so first add the percentage uncertainties inside the square root and then apply the power of one-half.
After finding the percentage uncertainty in v, multiply it by 21.1 m s⁻¹ to obtain the absolute uncertainty.
Round the absolute uncertainty appropriately, then quote v to the same decimal place.
walkthrough: The expression is v = (Tl/m)¹ᐟ². Start by combining the percentage uncertainties of the multiplied and divided measurements inside the brackets.
Add the percentage uncertainties: 5% + 1% + 2% = 8%.
The bracket is raised to the power one-half, so multiply the combined percentage uncertainty by ½: percentage uncertainty in v = ½ × 8% = 4%.
Write 4% as a decimal before calculating the absolute uncertainty: 4% = 4 ÷ 100 = 0.04.
Use the calculated speed from part (b)(i): Δv = 0.04 × 21.1 m s⁻¹.
Carry out the multiplication: Δv = 0.844 m s⁻¹.
Round the absolute uncertainty to one significant figure: Δv = 0.8 m s⁻¹.
The uncertainty is given to the nearest 0.1 m s⁻¹, so report the speed to the same decimal place.
The final result is v = (21.1 ± 0.8) m s⁻¹.

ai_rubric.observable: Combines the measurement uncertainties and accounts for the square root to obtain a percentage uncertainty in v of 4%, or a fractional uncertainty of 0.04.
Calculates the absolute uncertainty as approximately 0.84 m s⁻¹ from 0.04 × 21.1.
Reports v as (21.1 ± 0.8) m s⁻¹ with appropriate precision.
